what: Gaming and Leisure Properties owns casino buildings and leases them back to the operators who run them. It owns the real estate; Penn, Bally's, Boyd and others run the gambling.
customers: Casino operators across the United States, on very long triple-net leases.
money: loans made to operators for development
moat: Leases that run for decades with rent increases built in, on properties that hold gaming licences tied to the location. The tenant cannot move the casino elsewhere.
risks: Revenue depends on a small number of casino operators, so one failing matters
Regional casino revenue softens when consumer spending falls
opportunities: 11.6 times earnings with a 51.7% net margin and $929M of free cash flow
Analysts see about 29% upside, with 23 covering the stock
Rent escalators are contractual, so income rises each year without new investment
watch: Tenant rent coverage ratios and new acquisitions funded at attractive yields.
